title: bug: wrapper post-flight ends the claim loop when the seat attempt is already closed
description: FOLLOW-UP to task-2a7e0f5b (filed by its architect, 2026-09-13). That card makes the daemon close a seat's running/reconciling attempt at every hand-back (qa_reject, seat-freeing report_blocked, set_task_status, unblock_worker seat-only, the sweeps). The wrapper post-flight does not tolerate that today: scripts/moe-agent.sh finalize_postflight (~6733) calls finalize_attempt_rpc (~1968-1973), whose moe_attempt_read (~1872-1888) returns 1 ("ambiguous or missing open attempt") when the task has no non-closed attempt owned by this worker; the caller sets POSTFLIGHT_BREAK=true and the wrapper leaves its claim loop (~6797-6799) instead of claiming other work. The ps1 twin is Read-MoeAttempt (moe-agent.ps1 ~1279-1280) returning null so Send-MoeFinalize (~1363-1364) returns false. The role gate (~1969) confines this to WORKER seats. release_task already has this shape today; after task-2a7e0f5b a seat-freeing report_blocked (documented intent: "the seat was freed, go take other work", reportBlocked.ts ~266-271, docs/MCP_SERVER.md report_blocked Notes), a human set_task_status mid-session, a seat-only unblock_worker and the blocked-timeout park all end the worker wrapper's loop after its checkpoint landing. Expected: the wrapper treats "no open attempt owned by this worker" as a no-op success when the task is no longer assigned to this worker (or the pinned attempt reads back closed), and still hard-fails when the worker owns the task and its attempt is finalizing (the real landing boundary). Both twins + parity-check; wrapper-only, no daemon change. Related: task-49ec8755 owns launcher attempt integration (candidate/check-run/finalize wiring) — coordinate, do not duplicate.
definitionOfDone: finalize_attempt_rpc (moe-agent.sh) and Send-MoeFinalize (moe-agent.ps1) return success without calling finalize_attempt when the task is no longer assigned to this worker or its pinned attempt is closed, and the claim loop continues to the next claim_next_task
When the worker still owns the task and its attempt is finalizing, a failed finalize_attempt still sets POSTFLIGHT_BREAK exactly as today (existing behaviour, covered by a harness case)

scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 gain a freed-seat case (seat-freeing report_blocked, attempt closed by the daemon) that proves the loop continues; bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and the ps1 twin pass
docs/MCP_SERVER.md report_blocked Notes drop the interim sentence added by task-2a7e0f5b about the wrapper loop ending; docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md gains the symptom line

No code changes in this step; post ONE task comment with the findings. (a) scripts/moe-agent.sh finalize ladder, in order: role gate `[ "$ROLE" = worker ] && [ -n "${PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID:-}" ] || return 0`; `[WARN] Cannot finalize without pinned attempt identity.` (return 1); pinned-closed fast path (python over `$PROJECT/.moe/attempts/$MOE_ATTEMPT_ID.json`, phase=="closed" with matching id/taskId/workerId/generation → return 0); `moe_attempt_read "$MOE_ATTEMPT_ID" "$MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION"` (whole-glob parse, then `ambiguous or missing open attempt` / `identity` / `phase` / `stale identity`) → return 1; `[ "$phase" = finalizing ] || return 0`; 3-try `moe_evidence_rpc finalize_attempt` then `[WARN] finalize_attempt acknowledgement exhausted; stopping new-task loop (no repeated Git effect).` return 1; consumer `if ! finalize_postflight; then POSTFLIGHT_BREAK=true; fi`, reset `POSTFLIGHT_BREAK=false` per iteration, loop tail `if [ "$POSTFLIGHT_BREAK" = true ]; then break; fi` (break = script end = EXIT trap = deregister reason terminal_closed). moe_attempt_read is ALSO the fail-closed gate for pin_attempt_identity and record_candidate_rpc — it must not change. (b) scripts/moe-agent.ps1 twin: Read-MoeAttempt (reason spelled `phase or id`, not `phase`), Set-MoeAttemptIdentity, Send-MoeCandidate, Send-MoeFinalize (same ladder), Complete-MoePostflight; `$postflightBreak` is assigned once (`if (-not (Complete-MoePostflight)) { $postflightBreak=$true }`), never reset and never read — the only loop exit is `if ($moeStopLoop) { break }`, and `$moeStopLoop = $false` is reset per iteration. If 49ec8755 landed a fix, step 4 skips that part. (c) Ownership signal: both twins already hold the task's assignedWorkerId in post-flight from get_commit_scope (ps1 `$scope.AssignedWorkerId`; sh commit-scope parse; harness knob FAKE_SCOPE_ASSIGNED), but this plan deliberately keys on the pinned attempt's PHASE instead — say so in the comment, so QA reading DoD 1's 'no longer assigned to this worker' finds the reason: complete_task's own finalizing attempt sits on an already-unassigned task, so an assignment test would swallow the one case that must be acknowledged. (d) Harness facts step 2 builds on: the fake proxy's attemptFixture() writes `.moe/attempts/attempt-postflight.json` (id attempt-postflight, generation 7, phase running) only when the file is ABSENT; get_context flips it to finalizing only on its second call and only when FAKE_TASK_STATUS is REVIEW/DONE/ARCHIVED; FROZEN_MODE claim-missing withholds attemptId from the claim reply but the record is still written; the frozen driver hard-codes FAKE_TASK_STATUS REVIEW and deliberately asserts NO finalize row counts for missing-attempt/stale-attempt/claim-missing/claim-malformed/closed-attempt; sh run_scope_wrapper hard-codes `--no-loop --poll-interval 0`; `--loop --poll-interval 0` does not loop; ps1 has no scenario W (bash-only) and Invoke-WrapperProcess can only hard-kill on timeout; both harnesses hard-assert a commit-scope scenario count of 28 with different memberships (sh 'A-P, M2, R-U, W-Z, Z2, AA, AB'; ps1 'A-V, M2, X-Z, AA, AB'). (e) Baselines — run and record: `MOE_FROZEN_TEST_ONLY=finalize-loss bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` passed on the 49ec tree; the ps1 twin failed `6 !== 3`: the wrapper ran TWO iterations and ended by itself, and the second iteration logged `Cannot bind argument to parameter 'GitArgs' because it is an empty string.` for both the landing and the rescue ref — filed as task-32ecce5df28e4d72ad72b2ff079f53ba; note whether it still reproduces after 49ec8755 lands. (f) Daemon facts (read only): finalizeAttempt.ts returns idempotent success for a closed attempt BEFORE assertAttemptCurrent, refuses running/reconciling with ATTEMPT_NOT_FINALIZING, never checks workerId and fences by comparing the caller's attemptId/generation to the CURRENT attempt — so the wrapper must only ever acknowledge its exact pinned identity; claimNextTask.ts holds this worker's next claim only for its own phase-finalizing attempt; every supersede path (claim arm 3, release, purge, and after task-2a7e0f5b every hand-back) closes the old attempt in place first. State the corrected scope: a hand-back close of the PINNED attempt is already a no-op in both twins; this task closes the no-pin, identity-mismatch, reconciling and corrupt-sibling shapes, removes the no-pin hard stop, and fixes the ps1 loop-stop gap.

Phase 3 — Tests first, in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 (daemon-free). Fake-proxy additions, identical in BOTH harnesses: (a) claim counter `.moe/claim-count`, incremented on every claim_next_task; (b) `FAKE_CLAIM_SEQUENCE`, a comma list consumed by claim ordinal whose LAST element sticks once the list is exhausted — `task,idle` means claim 1 returns the normal task-postflight reply and every later claim returns `{ hasNext: false }`; the fake writes the marker `.moe/second-claim` on claim 2; (c) `FAKE_ATTEMPT_AFTER_CLI`, applied by the fake CLI as its last act (precedent: the frozen cliJs mutation): `closed` (phase closed in place), `reconciling`, `absent` (delete the file), `generation-bump` (same id, generation+1), `corrupt-sibling` (leave ours untouched and write `.moe/attempts/zzz-broken.json` containing `{not json`). The harnesses never set the attempt phase any other way in these groups. New runners (new code, budget it): sh `run_until_marker` — start the wrapper in the background with `--loop --poll-interval 1`, poll for `.moe/second-claim` for at most MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 60), then `kill -TERM` the process group, arm a `kill -9` watchdog, and report whether the marker appeared (do NOT reuse run_scope_wrapper, which forces `--no-loop`); ps1 `Invoke-WrapperUntilMarker` — Start-Process with `-Loop -PollInterval 1`, the same bounded poll, then `taskkill /T /F`. These cases assert only state produced BEFORE the kill; they never assert graceful teardown. Group '[freed seat]', FAKE_TASK_STATUS=BLOCKED (checkpoint exit, the scenario F shape), FAKE_CLAIM_SEQUENCE=task,idle; every case asserts exact counts: the marker exists, claim-count >= 2, exactly one wip checkpoint commit for task-postflight, ZERO finalize_attempt rows in `.moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl`. Cases: (1) `freed-closed` + FAKE_ATTEMPT_AFTER_CLI=closed — GUARD (pinned-closed fast path); also assert the log has NO notice line and NO `Attempt identity unavailable` line. (2) `freed-nopin` + FROZEN_MODE=claim-missing + FAKE_ATTEMPT_AFTER_CLI=absent — sh RED today (`Cannot finalize without pinned attempt identity.` breaks the loop, no marker); ps1 RED only on the notice line (its loop already continues); after the fix the log carries `[finalize] no finalizing attempt for this seat on task task-postflight` exactly once. (3) `freed-reconciling` + reconciling — sh RED (`phase` rejection breaks the loop); ps1 RED on the notice; after the fix the notice appears once. (4) `freed-corrupt-sibling` + corrupt-sibling — sh RED (the whole-glob parse fails and breaks the loop); ps1 RED on nothing today — keep it as a GUARD there, because step 4's new break makes ps1 capable of regressing; after the fix NO notice (the pinned attempt is running, a silent no-op). (5) `freed-generation-bump` + generation-bump — GUARD on both engines for loop continuation (sh `stale identity` today returns 1 and breaks → RED in sh), and after the fix the notice appears once and ZERO finalize rows — the wrapper must never acknowledge an identity it did not pin. Group '[finalizing seat]', FAKE_TASK_STATUS=REVIEW: (6) `finalizing-acked-continues` + FAKE_CLAIM_SEQUENCE=task,idle — exactly one finalize_attempt row with outcome landed and the pinned id/generation, marker exists — GUARD in sh, and in ps1 it proves the new break does not fire on success. The exhausted-ack guard (DoD 2) is the EXISTING frozen `finalize-loss` mode — do not duplicate it. Frozen-driver additions in both harnesses: assert ZERO finalize_attempt rows for missing-attempt, stale-attempt, claim-missing, claim-malformed and closed-attempt (closing the blind spot where a wrong ack would pass), and for claim-missing/claim-malformed also assert the new no-pin WARN line from step 3. Counters: bump the hard-coded commit-scope scenario count from 28 to 34 in BOTH files and extend each file's letter/name list in its failure message with the six new case names. Error handling in the runners: a missing marker fails the case with the last 40 log lines printed; the watchdog always fires even if the kill fails.

Phase 4a — scripts/moe-agent.sh: rewrite finalize_attempt_rpc as an exact-identity ladder. Doc comment: 'The post-flight acknowledges only the seat's own FINALIZING attempt, and only under the identity it pinned at claim time. A closed, running, reconciling, missing or no-longer-matching attempt is nothing to acknowledge and is a no-op success; a finalizing attempt with no pinned identity is never acknowledged and stops the loop; an exhausted acknowledgement stops the loop.' Ladder: (1) role gate — unchanged. (2) PIN PRESENT (`[ -n "$MOE_ATTEMPT_ID" ] && [ -n "$MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION" ]`): read ONLY `$PROJECT/.moe/attempts/$MOE_ATTEMPT_ID.json` with one python call that prints `<phase>` when id/taskId/workerId/generation all equal the pin and prints `mismatch` otherwise (missing file, unparseable JSON, or any identity field different — including a bumped generation). `closed` or `running` → return 0 silently (unchanged behaviour); `mismatch` or `reconciling` → print `[finalize] no finalizing attempt for this seat on task $PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID; nothing to acknowledge.` and return 0; `finalizing` → the existing 3-try `moe_evidence_rpc finalize_attempt` with the pinned id/generation (payload unchanged), exhausted → the existing `[WARN] finalize_attempt acknowledgement exhausted; stopping new-task loop (no repeated Git effect).` and return 1. The finalize path no longer calls moe_attempt_read, so a corrupt file for another task cannot affect it, and it never adopts any identity other than the pin. (3) NO PIN: python scan of `$PROJECT/.moe/attempts/*.json` that parses each file in its own try/except (an unreadable file is skipped with one stderr line naming it), keeps records with taskId==PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID and workerId==WORKER_ID, then phase=='finalizing'. None → the notice above and return 0. One or more → print `[WARN] finalize refused: finalizing attempt <id> on task <taskId> has no pinned identity; not acknowledging.` and return 1 (fail closed: never acknowledge an unpinned identity, and stop rather than livelock on the next claim's ATTEMPT_FINALIZING refusal). (4) Delete the `Cannot finalize without pinned attempt identity.` literal entirely, comments included. Leave moe_attempt_read, pin_attempt_identity and record_candidate_rpc byte-for-byte unchanged — candidate evidence keeps refusing on any unreadable or ambiguous record. Error handling: each python helper exits non-zero only on an interpreter failure, which the shell treats as `mismatch` for the pinned read (no-op) and as a hard failure for the no-pin scan (return 1 with the stderr line). Make step 2's sh cases (2)-(5) green; (1), (6) and every frozen mode stay green.

Phase 4b — scripts/moe-agent.ps1: mirror step 3 exactly. Send-MoeFinalize becomes: role gate (unchanged) → PIN PRESENT: read only `.moe/attempts/<pinnedId>.json` inside try/catch, compare id/taskId/workerId/generation to `$script:MoeAttemptId`/`$script:MoeAttemptGeneration`; closed/running → `$true` silently; mismatch (missing, unparseable, any field different) or reconciling → `Write-Host '[finalize] no finalizing attempt for this seat on task <id>; nothing to acknowledge.'` and `$true`; finalizing → the existing 3-try acknowledgement, exhausted → the existing `[WARN] finalize_attempt acknowledgement exhausted; stopping new-task loop (no repeated Git effect).` and `$false` → NO PIN: new `Find-MoeSeatFinalizingAttempts` (per-file try/catch, filter taskId then workerId then phase finalizing, returns an array) → empty: notice and `$true`; non-empty: `[WARN] finalize refused: finalizing attempt <id> on task <taskId> has no pinned identity; not acknowledging.` and `$false`. Delete the `Cannot finalize without pinned attempt identity.` literal entirely. Read-MoeAttempt, Set-MoeAttemptIdentity and Send-MoeCandidate stay unchanged. Loop-stop parity: add `$postflightBreak = $false` beside the per-iteration `$moeStopLoop = $false` reset, and make the loop tail `if ($postflightBreak -or $moeStopLoop) { break }`. A break falls into the existing finally (Stop-MoeGateChild, Invoke-MoeTeardownRescue, Complete-MoePostflight idempotent via `$script:MoeFinalizeDone`, Remove-MoeGateWorkspace, Remove-MoeLiveMarker, Invoke-MoeDeregister) — trace it once in the step report. Error handling: any exception inside Send-MoeFinalize's reads is caught and mapped exactly as in the bash twin (pinned read → mismatch → no-op; no-pin scan failure → `$false` with one `[WARN]` line); nothing escapes to skip deregistration. Expected result: ps1 frozen `finalize-loss` turns from RED (`6 !== 3`) to GREEN because the loop now stops after the exhausted acknowledgement; step 2's ps1 cases (2), (3), (5) turn green on the notice line; (4) and (6) stay green.

Phase 4c — Parity. scripts/tests/parity-check.sh auto-compares only the MOE_COMMIT_ / MOE_ATTR_ / MOE_CHECKPOINT_ / MOE_ATTRIBUTION_ token sets; scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1 compares those four plus a bare MOE_RESCUE_REF (sh carries that one as a fixed-list item). Every other literal is a fixed list checked with a plain substring search in BOTH wrappers (sh `require_both LABEL NEEDLE` via grep -Fq; ps1 `$required` ordered groups), and both scripts read only scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 — never the harnesses and never each other. Register, in BOTH lists (the existing log-prefix / prose groups; no new category): `[finalize] no finalizing attempt for this seat on task`, `has no pinned identity; not acknowledging.`, `finalize_attempt acknowledgement exhausted; stopping new-task loop`, and the prefix `Attempt identity unavailable:` (still present in both twins' unchanged candidate reads; the reasons after it differ in spelling between twins, so register only the prefix). Do NOT register `Cannot finalize without pinned attempt identity.` (deleted from both twins) and do NOT register any FAKE_* name (harness-only — both checks would report it missing from both wrappers). Introduce no new MOE_* token. Run `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` and `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1`; both must pass. Prove the guard once: delete the notice literal from one wrapper, confirm BOTH parity scripts fail, restore it.

Phase 5 — Regression on a quiet box (fleet idle; these harnesses flake under vitest load). Run `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` and `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/postflight.ps1`; both must end with their PASS line and a commit-scope scenario count of 34. Expected deltas versus the pre-change baseline recorded in step 1, per frozen mode, on both engines: finalize-loss 3 finalize rows and a loop stop (ps1 newly green); finalize-loss-once 2 rows; missing-attempt, stale-attempt, closed-attempt 0 rows (pinned read → mismatch or closed); claim-missing and claim-malformed 0 rows plus the no-pin WARN; every completion mode whose candidate evidence is unavailable still fails closed with MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE and a rescue ref, because record_candidate_rpc / Send-MoeCandidate were not touched. If the GitArgs second-landing failure (task-32ecce5df28e4d72ad72b2ff079f53ba) still reproduces, it must not be hidden: note in the step report that the ps1 finalize-loss run now stops after iteration 1 and link the card. Then run both parity checks again. Record exact counts and the two PASS lines; rerun a flaky harness alone before concluding.

Phase 6 — Docs. docs/CONFIGURATION.md, '### Frozen quality-gate candidates' (added by task-49ec8755): one paragraph with the finalize rule — the post-flight acknowledges only the seat's own finalizing attempt under the identity pinned at claim time; a closed attempt (for example one the daemon closed when the task was handed back), a running, reconciling or missing attempt, or one whose record no longer matches the pin is nothing to acknowledge and the worker keeps claiming; a finalizing attempt with no pinned identity is never acknowledged and stops the loop; an exhausted acknowledgement stops the loop — in both wrappers. docs/MCP_SERVER.md, moe.report_blocked — three edit sites that promise a nextAction on the freed arm: the 'Seat-freeing' Notes bullet (`nextAction` points at `moe.claim_next_task` so the seat takes other work), the nextAction Notes bullet (a seat-freed block points at `moe.claim_next_task`), and the Returns block. reportBlocked.ts emits NO nextAction on the freed arm; document instead `seatFreed: true`, `workerStatus: 'IDLE'`, `sessionHandoff { action: 'END_SESSION', taskId, workerId, reason }` — present on a freed seat unless the seat worker already holds another task — and `blockResolution` (the auto-unblock text naming the prerequisite ids, or the human escape via moe.set_task_status), which the Returns block omits today. Interim sentence (DoD 4): grep report_blocked Notes for a sentence saying the worker wrapper ends its claim loop after a seat-freeing block; if task-2a7e0f5b added one, remove it and quote it in the step report; if none landed, say so and add nothing. docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md under '## Task Sync Issues', next to '### `unblock_worker` no longer clears the block (RE-BLOCK)': a `### Worker wrapper stopped after a blocked or handed-back task` block. **Symptom:** the wrapper exited instead of claiming more work. Lines that mean a real stop: `finalize_attempt acknowledgement exhausted` (a finalizing attempt could not be acknowledged), `finalize refused: finalizing attempt ... has no pinned identity`, and `MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE` on a completion whose attempt was unavailable. Lines that are benign: `[finalize] no finalizing attempt for this seat on task ...`, and at pre-flight `Missing/stale attempt identity; candidate completion will fail closed.` when a resume found no single open attempt. Fix: relaunch the seat; a stuck finalizing attempt is cleared by moe.finalize_attempt with its exact id and generation, or closed by the next claim of that task by another seat.

Phase 7+8 — Adversarial self-review, then complete. Answer in the task comment: (1) FENCE — the wrapper acknowledges only its exact pinned id/generation; prove with case (5) freed-generation-bump and the frozen stale-attempt mode (0 finalize rows) that a bumped or foreign record is never acknowledged, since the daemon itself never checks workerId. (2) RACE — the daemon closes or supersedes the pinned attempt between the disk read and the RPC: every supersede path closes the old attempt first, and finalize_attempt on a closed attempt is idempotent success before the fence, so the practical outcome is success; a refusal (ATTEMPT_NOT_FINALIZING / ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED) is still treated as failure and stops the loop — record this as a knowingly accepted residual and why no error-codeName parsing was added. (3) NO PIN + FINALIZING — the wrapper stops rather than acknowledging an identity it never pinned; say why stopping beats both acknowledging (fence) and continuing (the next claim would be refused with ATTEMPT_FINALIZING every poll). (4) CORRUPT FILES — the pinned read opens one file, so an unrelated corrupt record cannot affect finalize; the no-pin scan skips unreadable files by name; candidate evidence still fails closed on any unreadable record because moe_attempt_read / Read-MoeAttempt were not changed. (5) ps1 BREAK — trace that `$postflightBreak` is reset each iteration and that a break runs the whole finally, deregistration included. (6) RESUME onto a reconciling or closed attempt — the pin fails at pre-flight (unchanged), the CLI runs, a checkpoint exit then finds no finalizing attempt and continues; a completion exit in that state still fails closed at record_candidate by design. (7) Ctrl+C mid-finalize — the EXIT trap / finally re-enter the idempotent finalize. (8) Hidden defect — confirm the GitArgs second-landing card (task-32ecce5df28e4d72ad72b2ff079f53ba) is linked if it still reproduces. Then rerun both harnesses and both parity checks, call moe.declare_files for every path touched, and moe.complete_task with `verification: { command: 'MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh', exitCode: 0, outputTail }` (ending in the PASS line) and a summary naming the exact-identity finalize rule, the no-pin stop, the ps1 loop-stop fix and the two new harness groups.

comments.author: agent
comments.content: ARCHITECT NOTE (operator session), 2026-09-13 ~21:15Z — corrected premise before planning. Read against task-49ec8755's in-flight working tree (functions absent at HEAD): both wrappers ALREADY treat a pinned attempt that reads back phase closed with matching id/taskId/workerId/generation as a no-op success (finalize_attempt_rpc fast path; Send-MoeFinalize fast path), and a running attempt never sends the RPC. So the daemon's close-on-hand-back of the pinned attempt (task-2a7e0f5b) does NOT end the loop on checkpoint exits. What still ends it: no pinned identity (claim reply without attemptId from an older daemon; a resume onto an attempt already closed or parked reconciling), a pinned record rewritten to reconciling, a file-absent/identity-mismatch read, and a corrupt attempt file for ANY task (both twins parse every file before filtering by taskId). Opposite defect in ps1:  is set by Complete-MoePostflight but never read, so a real finalize failure livelocks on ATTEMPT_FINALIZING refusals (MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=claim-failed every poll) instead of stopping like bash. The plan therefore keys the no-op on the attempt PHASE (acknowledge only the seat's own finalizing attempt on the task, found on disk by taskId+workerId whether pinned or not), not on task assignment — a finalizing attempt's task is already unassigned by complete_task, so assignment alone would swallow the one case that must be acknowledged. DoD 1 is satisfied by that stronger rule. Wrapper-only; no daemon change needed (no MCP attempt read exists and none is required). Line numbers in the description are stale; grep anchors are in the plan.

OVERLAP NOTICE from task-49ec8755's rework (worker-a7127038, 2026-09-14). QA rejection issue 2 is this card's corrected scope, so 49ec8755 now implements the finalize ladder in both wrappers, following step-3/4 of this plan.
Pinned identity: only the pinned record is read. Finalizing gets up to 3 identical tries, and exhaustion stops the loop. Closed or running is a silent no-op. Reconciling, missing or mismatched logs `[finalize] no finalizing attempt for this seat on task <id>; nothing to acknowledge.` and succeeds.
No pin: a tolerant per-file scan looks for this seat's finalizing attempt on the task. If there is none, the notice above. If there is one, `[WARN] finalize refused: finalizing attempt ... has no pinned identity; not acknowledging.` and the loop stops.
Harness arms (sh and ps1): WORKING checkpoint and autoCommit=false exits under --loop with a reconciling or unpinned attempt. The unpinned arm also carries a corrupt sibling attempt file. Each arm asserts that a second claim happens and that zero finalize_attempt calls were made.
Not covered here: moe_attempt_read's whole-glob parse on the gated candidate path (a corrupt sibling still fails a gated completion closed), the freed-seat report_blocked case, and the MCP_SERVER.md and TROUBLESHOOTING.md edits. The exact coverage list will be in 49ec8755's completion summary.

comments.content:
COORDINATION NOTE (architect-operator, 2026-09-14). task-49ec8755 was rejected by qa-f0f9ea9e at 19:10Z with issues that overlap this card:
- Its issue 2 is this card's core fix: finalize returns failure when the identity is unpinned or the attempt phase is not running/finalizing, before checking whether anything is finalizing; only a failed acknowledgement for an existing finalizing attempt may stop the loop.
- Its requested harness modes (a WORKING checkpoint and an autoCommit=false exit under --loop with a reconciling or missing identity, asserting the loop continues and zero finalize_attempt calls) overlap this plan's step 2.
This card depends on task-49ec8755, so that rework lands first. When claiming: in step 1, compare the landed rework against this plan, skip every part it already delivered, and keep only what remains — typically the exact-identity no-op for a generation mismatch, the no-pin finalizing stop, the ps1 $postflightBreak wiring if still dead, the parity literals and the docs. Say in the step-1 comment what was skipped and why. If nothing remains, report that and complete with the verification run.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 9 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Corrected scope: the card's premise (a hand-back close of the seat's attempt ends the worker loop) is already false in task-49ec8755's design — both twins turn a pinned attempt that reads back closed into a no-op, and a running attempt never sends the RPC. What still ends the sh loop: a missing pin, a pinned record rewritten to reconciling or to another generation, and a corrupt attempt file for ANY task (the whole-glob parse in moe_attempt_read). In ps1 the opposite defect: $postflightBreak is never read, so a real exhausted acknowledgement does not stop the loop. Chosen rule: acknowledge only the seat's own FINALIZING attempt under its exact pinned identity, read from that one file; everything else is a no-op success; a finalizing attempt with no pin is never acknowledged and stops the loop. Rejected (from plan critique): an identity-blind taskId+workerId+phase scan that adopts whatever finalizing record it finds — it drops the generation fence, and because finalize_attempt never checks workerId and fences only against the CURRENT attempt, a stale runner could close a live runner's attempt. Rejected: keying on 'task no longer assigned to this worker' (DoD 1's wording) — complete_task's own finalizing attempt sits on an already-unassigned task. Rejected: per-file hardening of moe_attempt_read — it is the fail-closed gate for candidate evidence and a skipped corrupt record for THIS task would let a pin through. Rejected: parsing finalize error codeNames (the wrappers' RPC helpers discard error.data, and every supersede closes the old attempt first). Rejected: any daemon change (card rail).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Attempt reads in the wrappers are disk reads of .moe/attempts/<id>.json, the daemon's own persisted records; setAttemptPhase rewrites a record in place keeping id/taskId/workerId/generation, and a new generation always gets a new id, so a same-id record with a different generation is not a legitimate daemon state. finalize_attempt returns idempotent success for a closed attempt before its fence, refuses running/reconciling with ATTEMPT_NOT_FINALIZING, never checks workerId and compares the caller's id/generation to the CURRENT attempt. claim_next_task holds a worker's next claim only for its own finalizing attempt. The harness fake proxy writes the attempt fixture only when absent and flips it to finalizing only for REVIEW/DONE/ARCHIVED on the second get_context; the frozen driver fixes REVIEW and skips finalize-row counts for the identity-failure modes; no existing case proves a second claim after post-flight, and ps1 has no graceful-interrupt primitive outside the frozen driver, so the new runners end the loop with a kill after a marker and assert only pre-kill state. The critique's run of the ps1 frozen finalize-loss mode also exposed an unrelated second-landing failure (empty GitArgs) that the new break would hide; it is filed separately.
planningNotes.risks: (1) Line drift and double-editing: every symbol here lives in task-49ec8755's uncommitted tree; step 1 re-reads the landed revision by grep anchors and skips anything 49ec already fixed. (2) Loop-plus-kill harness cases are the flakiest pattern; they need a quiet box, a bounded marker poll and a watchdog, and assert only state written before the kill. (3) DoD 1 is met by a stronger phase- and identity-based rule than its assignment wording; step 1's comment explains why. (4) DoD 4 presumes an interim docs sentence from task-2a7e0f5b; that task has been told its premise is false, so most likely no sentence lands and step 7 records that. (5) Stopping on a finalizing attempt with no pin is a behaviour choice that removes a livelock but ends a seat; it is documented in TROUBLESHOOTING with the fix. (6) The GitArgs second-landing defect is out of scope and tracked on its own card so the new ps1 break does not bury it.
